candidates.title: Skill Weaving: Efficient LLM Improvement via Modular Skillpacks
candidates.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
candidates.abstract: Large language models increasingly require specialization across diverse domains, yet existing approaches struggle to balance multi-domain capacities with strict memory and inference constraints. In this work, we introduce SkillWeave, a modular improvement framework that enables LLMs to specialize under fixed memory budgets. SkillWeave partitions full capabilities of a general-purpose model into skillpacks -- lightweight, domain-specific delta modules -- that reorganize and refine the model's internal knowledge. For efficient deployment, SkillWeave integrates SkillZip to compress skillpacks into compact and inference-ready format, enabling strong multi-domain performance with low-latency execution. On multi-task and agentic benchmarks, a 9B SkillWeave model outperforms several baselines and even surpasses a 32B monolithic LLM, while achieving up to 4x speedup.
candidates.reason: SkillWeaveは固定メモリ予算下で分野別の軽量deltaモジュールskillpackを構成し、SkillZipで推論用の圧縮形式へ変換する。一次要旨では9B構成が32B単体モデルを複数課題で上回り、最大4倍の実行高速化を報告。主眼は分野特化能力だが、推論時メモリと低遅延のためのモジュール圧縮を明示するため収録対象。

candidates.title: Lightweight Large-Model Inference with Privacy Protection for Edge IoT Systems
candidates.venue: 2026 9th International Conference on Advanced Electronic Technology, Computers and Software Engineering (AETCSE)
candidates.abstract: Edge IoT systems increasingly require real-time intelligent services, yet direct deployment of large language models (LLMs) or multimodal foundation models on constrained edge devices faces severe memory, latency, and privacy risks. Cloud-only inference pipelines can simplify deployment but often violate data minimization requirements in sensitive scenarios such as healthcare monitoring and smart homes. This paper proposes a privacy-preserving lightweight large-model inference framework for edge IoT systems that jointly optimizes model compression, collaborative inference, and secure execution. The framework combines mixed-precision quantization, structured pruning, and knowledge distillation to derive compact edge students, while a federated inference coordinator exchanges only protected intermediate statistics rather than raw data. Differential privacy is introduced for controllable leakage mitigation, and trusted execution environments (TEEs) are used to isolate security-critical operators and keys. A latency-aware policy engine dynamically selects local-only, edge-only, or edge-cloud fallback paths according to device load and privacy budget. Experiments on a heterogeneous edge cluster show that the proposed method reduces model storage by over 80% and cuts end-to-end inference latency by up to 75% compared with an FP16 baseline while maintaining competitive accuracy under strict privacy constraints. The results demonstrate practical feasibility for privacy-sensitive edge intelligence upgrades.
candidates.reason: エッジIoTのLLM/基盤モデル推論向けに混合精度量子化・構造化枝刈り・知識蒸留で小型studentを作り、プライバシー予算と端末負荷に応じてローカル・エッジ・クラウド経路を切り替える。一次要旨ではモデル保存容量80%以上削減、FP16基準のE2E推論遅延最大75%削減を報告。推論圧縮と分散配置の直接的システム貢献。
